colors.name: Voltage Violet
colors.role: Primary action buttons, active nav items, key links, brand emphasis - the single chromatic pulse of the interface; everything else defers to it

colors.name: Deep Iris
colors.role: Dark section backgrounds, hero canvas, high-contrast text on light surfaces - the midnight counterpart that anchors alternating dark bands

colors.name: Signal Red
colors.role: Promotional accents, sale/urgency indicators, highlight strokes - used sparingly to flag attention without competing with the primary violet

colors.name: Lilac Whisper
colors.role: Soft card and container borders - a low-contrast violet edge that brands outlines without adding visual weight

colors.name: Periwinkle Mist
colors.role: Cooler card border tone for grouping and container edges - second step in the violet border scale for layered cards

colors.name: Coral Burst
colors.role: Error and warning badge fills, alert pills - warm contrast against the cool violet system

colors.name: Aqua Pop
colors.role: Decorative badge backgrounds, hero trust-pill fill - cool cyan that brightens dark sections

colors.name: Ink Black
colors.role: Primary body and heading text, dominant border color, icon strokes - the near-black that carries all readable content

colors.name: Carbon
colors.role: Secondary text, muted nav, supporting borders - the mid-gray step between ink and white

colors.name: Pure White
colors.role: Page and card backgrounds, text on dark surfaces, button fills for ghost variants

colors.name: Frost Blue
colors.role: Subtle surface tint for alternating bands, header backgrounds - barely-there cool wash

colors.name: Linen Gray
colors.role: Table dividers, hairline borders in data-heavy layouts - a cool neutral that doesn't fight the violet palette

fonts.name: Haffer
fonts.role: Single-family system for everything from body to display. Weight 400 carries body, nav, and table text; weight 600 handles headings, buttons, and emphasis. The custom geometric construction gives a contemporary financial-tech voice - rounder apertures than Inter, tighter terminals than Geist.

components.name: Ghost Action Button
components.role: Secondary CTA paired beside a primary

components.name: Trust Badge Pill
components.role: Social proof or category label above hero headline

components.name: Pricing Tier Card
components.role: Product plan comparison on pricing sections

components.name: Inline Feature Icon
components.role: Category indicator on pricing and feature cards

do: Use Voltage Violet (#471cff) exclusively for the single most important action per screen - never split attention across multiple violet CTAs
Set card borders to Lilac Whisper (#dbd3ff) or Periwinkle Mist (#bbc5fa) instead of neutral gray to reinforce brand identity at every edge
Set all buttons to 400px border-radius - pill shapes are non-negotiable in this system and signal action
Tighten letter-spacing progressively: -0.030em at 16px, -0.033em at 26-30px, -0.045em at 48px+
Alternate between white and Deep Iris (#0f0733) sections to create rhythm - never let two dark sections sit adjacent without a white break
Anchor dark sections with white text at full opacity; use Lilac Whisper (#dbd3ff) for secondary text on dark rather than dimmed white
Use Signal Red (#eb0130) only for discount badges and urgency - never as a replacement for the primary action color
doNot: Don't introduce new hues - the system is binary: violet accents on white, or white on Deep Iris
Don't use drop shadows on components other than the pricing card stack - depth should come from color and border
Don't use sharp 0px or minimal 4px corner radii on cards - 16px is the minimum card radius and buttons must stay pill-shaped
Don't place body text below 14px or above 18px - the system avoids both micro-copy and large body type
Don't use #18181f and #000000 interchangeably - #000000 is reserved for navigation chrome; body text uses #18181f
Don't add gradients - the system is flat by design; depth comes from violet-to-Deep-Iris section contrast
Don't use weight 400 for headings or weight 600 for body - the binary weight assignment is part of the typographic signature
